newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Extra Chohung Bank shares to be open to foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Extra Chohung Bank shares to be open to foreigners.

text.p: South Korea's Securities Supervisory Board said on Tuesday that 4.39 percent of Chohung Bank's outstanding common shares would become available for foreign investment from June 26.
If the additional stake is wholly purchased by foreigners, combined foreign shareholding in the bank would reach 28 percent, compared with the uniform 23 percent ceiling on the foreign ownership.
Foreigners now own 23.61 percent of Chohung Bank but this includes 11.69 percent owned by foreigners through investment in depositary receipts issued abroad.
South Korean companies can open up an additional amount of shares to foreigners, if their foreign ownership includes stake holders from the beginning or holders of equity-linked securities abroad.
